clue.text: Mark, for example, place to visit that is on record

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece on another follows it, so the record comes first

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record

indicators.note: one piece visiting another goes inside it, here the place abbreviation stays within the Latin 'that is'

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A music fan named Mark plans a pilgrimage to a spot linked with a famous recording.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' poses as a verb or a name in a guide, but it is the Gospel writer, a follower of Jesus.
explanation.definitionFit: Mark the Evangelist was a follower of Jesus, so he is an example of a follower.

clue.text: Shakes off flipping journalist in bar

indicators.note: flipping turns the whole assembly over, so it is read from right to left
the journalist goes in the bar, inside its letters

parts.note: bar as a preposition means except, as does save
ED, short for editor, is the crossword's usual journalist

explanation.surface: Someone escapes a tiresome reporter who keeps turning up in the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' sounds like a mild British swear word, but it reverses SEDAVE (ED in SAVE) to give the answer. 'bar' is the preposition meaning 'except', not a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: To shake off a pursuer is to elude or escape them, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Initially trailing behind, character makes winning move

indicators.note: initially picks out just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: the behind is the rump, the backside
a card is an eccentric person, a character

explanation.surface: An outsider who was at first trailing makes the decisive move.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing a trump card is a decisive stroke that wins the day, so it names a winning move.

clue.text: Less adventurous travellers a ferry carries

indicators.note: the words carry the answer within them, running across travellers, a and ferry

explanation.surface: Cautious tourists prefer to go by ferry rather than fly.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone less adventurous takes fewer risks, so they are more cautious or more secure.

clue.text: Caught by woman's husband burying ones treasure

indicators.note: by means next to, so the catch letter stands beside the rest

parts.note: C is the cricket scoring abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: the woman's and husband pieces together bury the numeral, enclosing it

parts.note: woman's, belonging to her, is hers
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wife's husband is caught hiding his prized possessions.
explanation.definitionFit: To treasure something is to hold it dear, which is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Key doubt about king and queen's escort

parts.note: E is a musical key

indicators.note: the doubt word goes about the king, surrounding the R

parts.note: a query is a question or doubt
R, from Latin rex, is the abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A crucial uncertainty surrounds who will accompany the royal couple.
explanation.walkthrough: An equerry is an officer attending a member of the British royal family.
explanation.definitionFit: An equerry is a royal household officer who attends on and accompanies the monarch.

clue.text: Name no longer used by one country for genocide

parts.note: ex- describes something former, no longer in use
a term is a word or name for something
I is the Roman numeral for one
a nation is a country

explanation.surface: A people's former name was dropped by a state committing mass murder.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'Name no longer used' but the answer puts the former marker before the name.
explanation.definitionFit: Genocide is the attempted wiping out of a whole people, their total destruction.

clue.text: Chat oddly and leer when drunk in an unfriendly way

indicators.note: drunk suggests these letters stagger into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A drunk talking strangely and leering comes across as hostile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when drunk' rearranges CHAT, ODDLY and LEER; 'oddly' looks like an alternate-letter signal but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting without warmth or sympathy is acting in an unfeeling, unfriendly manner.

clue.text: Appear to include old part of UK in official record

indicators.note: the appearance word includes the other pieces, holding them within it

parts.note: to look is to appear, seem
GB, Great Britain, is the main part of the United Kingdom

explanation.surface: A document seems to cover an outdated region of Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A logbook is an official register, such as a ship's log or a British vehicle registration document.

clue.text: Obscure extracts from paper in middle of speech

indicators.note: the extracts go in the middle letters, sitting between them
middle of takes the central letters of the word speech

parts.note: clips are cuttings taken from a newspaper

explanation.surface: Quotations from a newspaper interrupt an address and make its meaning murky.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective but is a verb here, meaning to hide from view.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to block out or overshadow something, so it obscures it.

clue.text: Result of such a lot of lies being ignored at first

indicators.note: the opening letter is ignored, leaving the rest

parts.note: a tissue of lies is a mass of falsehoods

explanation.surface: Outcome of a stream of untruths that went unnoticed early on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A tissue of lies' is an idiom for a web of untruths.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is an outcome or consequence, as in the issue of a dispute.

clue.text: Adulterous couple: man and short Swedish girl?

parts.note: a couple is two
Tim is a man's name

indicators.note: short means cut off before the final letter

parts.note: Inga is a Scandinavian girl's name

explanation.surface: An unfaithful pair: a man and a petite Scandinavian woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-timing describes deceiving a partner by seeing someone else, being unfaithful.

clue.text: Boy going around in the buff?

definitions.text: Boy going around in the buff?

indicators.note: going around suggests letters turning about into a new order

parts.note: Dustin is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A lad wandering about without clothes on.
explanation.walkthrough: The boy's name DUSTIN is rearranged; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A naturist goes about unclothed, which is exactly what being in the buff means.

clue.text: This German's possibly drunk while playing with gun

indicators.note: playing with the letters suggests toying with them into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A German drinks heavily while fooling about with a firearm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like the anagram signal but belongs to the definition: this is a thing one drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: Glühwein is German mulled wine, a drink, so it is what a German might have drunk.

clue.text: Diamonds cut outside capital of Angola for free

parts.note: D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

indicators.note: the cut word sits outside, wrapping round the capital letter

parts.note: to etch is to cut into a surface

indicators.note: capital of means the first letter of Angola

explanation.surface: Gems cut abroad around an African capital are released.
explanation.definitionFit: To detach something is to unfasten or free it.

clue.text: Impudence of author on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means as broadcast, so the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: an author is the originator or source of something

explanation.surface: A writer is cheeky during a broadcast interview.
explanation.walkthrough: In a British non-rhotic accent the word for origin is said just like the cheek word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauce is informal British for cheek or insolence.

clue.text: Signs oddly overlooked — type on the streets

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters of signs are overlooked, keeping the second and fourth

parts.note: print is type, printed letters

explanation.surface: Notices posted in public are ignored by some passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the streets' means out and available, as a published book is.
explanation.definitionFit: A publication that is available to buy is out in the shops, published and on sale.

clue.text: What biker might assume is a swimmer

definitions.meaning: assume means put on, and a motorcyclist typically wears a hide coat
a kind of fish with tough skin

explanation.definitionFit: A biker's typical coat shares its name with a tough-skinned fish.

clue.text: View in which we see extremely unusual flower

indicators.note: the view is the place in which the other letters are seen, containing them

parts.note: a vista is a view

indicators.note: extremely means the extreme ends of unusual

explanation.surface: A view with a rare bloom in it.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'flower' is something that flows, a river: the Vistula runs through Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: Crosswords use flower for a river, something that flows, and the Vistula is Poland's longest river.

clue.text: Imperfection of a kind accepted by God

indicators.note: the god takes in the other word, so it sits inside

parts.note: a deity is a god
a form is a kind or type

explanation.surface: A flaw of some sort is tolerated by the Almighty.
explanation.definitionFit: A deformity is a malformation, a physical flaw.

clue.text: During swindle note aberration

indicators.note: during places the note within the swindle

parts.note: a sting is a confidence trick
ray is a note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A con trick featuring a musical note goes off course.
explanation.definitionFit: Straying is wandering from the right path, a deviation or departure from the norm.

clue.text: Incurable oldie they'd now treated

indicators.note: treated suggests the letters are processed into a new form

explanation.surface: An elderly person is beyond cure despite being given treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Dyed-in-the-wool describes someone thoroughly set in their ways, inveterate and beyond reform.

clue.text: Lose guide after trip that's raved about

indicators.note: after a trip the letters have stumbled into disorder

explanation.surface: Losing the tour guide after a holiday is something people rave about.
explanation.definitionFit: To eulogise is to praise highly, so something eulogised has been raved about.

clue.text: Vegetable in demand, one lad eats

indicators.note: the lad eats the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: a son is a lad, a boy
call means demand, as in no call for it
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: One lad eats a vegetable that is popular.
explanation.definitionFit: A scallion is a spring onion, a vegetable.

clue.text: Rugby players regularly heard breaking into catchy refrains

indicators.note: the selection breaks into the refrains, going inside them

parts.note: hooks are catchy musical phrases

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of heard

explanation.surface: Fans singing tuneful choruses interrupt rugby.
explanation.walkthrough: A hooker is the rugby forward in the middle of the front row of the scrum.
explanation.definitionFit: Hookers are forwards in a rugby scrum, so they are rugby players.

clue.text: Stupid officer, idiot primarily into money

indicators.note: the officer and initial go into the money

parts.note: dosh is British slang for money
Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer

indicators.note: primarily means first, so only the first letter of idiot is used

explanation.surface: A foolish officer is basically a moron about cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Doltish means like a dolt, a blockhead, so slow-witted.

clue.text: Almost back win that ousts current president

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter goes

parts.note: the rear is the back

indicators.note: ousts means the current symbol is driven out of the win word

parts.note: to gain is to win
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A near victory that unseats the sitting leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States.

clue.text: Different sorts of energy raised to land right reward

indicators.note: the right letter lands inside the turned word
raised in a down clue means read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: zip is pep or vigour, and E is the physics symbol for energy, two different sorts
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Several kinds of power are lifted to secure a just award.
explanation.definitionFit: A prize is something won as a reward.
